Visionary

/VIZH-uh-nair-ee/ - the stress falls on VIZH · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Visionary means boldly imaginative about what the future could become.

Bankers laughed in 1971 when the visionary economist predicted that shoppers would one day wave a plastic card instead of counting out bills.

Worked Example

In 1919, a visionary school superintendent argued that every child would someday need to type, and ordered typewriters for classrooms that still lacked electric light. The purchase was ridiculed as folly; two generations later it looked like a prophecy filed early.

Visionary praises imagination aimed at the future - seeing what could exist decades before it does. It differs from fanciful, which imagines freely without caring whether the vision could ever come true.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

farsighted: seeing consequences well ahead

prophetic: seeming to foretell what actually came

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

shortsighted: blind to what is coming

unimaginative: unable to picture anything new

Where it sits · how far beyond the present it sees — forward-looking → visionary → prophetic

forward-looking vs. visionary: Forward-looking credits someone with planning ahead; visionary goes further, crediting them with imagining a future others cannot yet see.

prophetic vs. visionary: Prophetic outruns visionary: the visionary designer imagines what the future could become, while a prophetic warning turns out to state what the future actually did.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vis-

Root — vis-: to see

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or state of

Suffix — -ary

Suffix — -ary: relating to, one who

Put it together

Put it together: Vis- (to see) + -ion (act or state of) + -ary (relating to) = relating to seeing. Latin videre, 'to see,' gives English its vision; add -ary and you get the person or plan that sees - not the room in front of them, but the decade ahead.

Use the root in a new word: envision

Use the root in a new word: envision: Architects envision the finished bridge long before the first cable is strung.

Word Choice

admiring / formal

Visionary is high praise for future-facing imagination that history may prove right. Its unit-mates split the territory: audacious praises the nerve of a bold move made now, and idealistic describes devotion to principles that may float above the facts. Call a plan visionary only when its boldness lies in seeing what is coming.
